No bit coins are not based on thin air. Like any other currency they are a derivative of a underlying good and service. Just as many currencies are based on the value of gold, Bit coins are based on the value of the electrical power needed to mine the bit currency. If the power to run all the mining rigs costs more than the value of the bit coins it produces then no body will mine for bit currency. But if the cost of electricity is less than the value of the bit coin then mining will take place. The greater the positive cost differential between electrical power and the purchase price of mining equipment the more mining will take place. As the value of Bit Currencies falls less mining will take place. And since the cost of the production of electricity varies greatly around the world, some places have an advantage in mining crypto currency while others don't.

Perfect example is comparing the mining of crypto currency in Portland Oregon and Silicon Valley. Average cost of power in Portland is 11 cents per kilowatt hour. The average price of Electricity in San Jose California is almost 15 cents per kilo watt hour. So you will able to mine 125-130 bit coins in Portland to the 100 bit coins in San Jose.
